https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/25/isra.text: All West Bank land crossings are set to be closed on Tuesday as Israel holds legislative elections, the Israeli military has said.In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers to and from all of Judea, Samaria, and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings throughout election day."It added that from Sunday through Monday, Palestinian workers would also not be permitted to enter Judea, Samaria or the Jordan Valley to work, "with the exception of industrial zones and a few other approved areas."The move comes as part of a wider clampdown in the occupied West Bank after two Israeli soldiers were killed by Palestinian gunmen in the city of Hebron earlier this week.Following the shooting, the IDF said its forces were surrounding Hebron as soldiers conducted search operations. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had instructed the military to "cordon off the city" and take "additional security measures" in the area.Israel has since begun demolishing buildings as residents have been removed from the region.The Palestinian News Agency (Wafa) reported on Sunday that more than 200 families have been displaced in Hebron over the past three days, with around 2,500 people forcibly removed from their homes in the al-Jilda and Ain Deir Baha areas.Israeli forces also detained 20 people across the wider Hebron Governorate on Sunday as part of the crackdown, the report said.The IDF said it had launched a "targeted operation" around Hebron that aimed to dismantle "terrorist infrastructure" and prevent future attacks."To reduce the risk to civilians, civilians were permitted to temporarily leave the area through designated screening points. No civilians were forced to evacuate," it said in a statement.The military also confirmed that a number of structures in Hebron had been demolished, saying they had posed a "security threat.""All other structures demolished in the area were also built illegally, and their demolition was carried out in accordance with international law in order to enforce law and order and remove potential security threats," the IDF said.B'Tselem, an Israeli human rights group, has condemned Israeli "plans to forcibly displace Palestinian residents from their homes and carry out widespread destruction in the area."The group has also called on the international community to "act immediately" to put a stop to Israel's campaign in Hebron.Anti-government protestsIt comes as thousands of people took to the streets of Tel Aviv on Saturday to protest against the government ahead of Tuesday's election.Demonstrators reportedly marched from Rabin Square in the city centre towards Hostages Square, renamed in the wake of Hamas' 7 October 2023 attacks on Israel.The rally was organised by the October Council, a group set up by families of victims and hostages taken by militants during the attacks."This evening has given us tremendous strength, but our struggle is not yet over," the group wrote in a post on social media on Sunday. "We must now channel the incredible energy from the square into action. This coming Tuesday, we’re all going out to vote."

https://www.dw.com/en/german-police-resp.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PkYU Prefer DW on Google Police responded to bomb threats against multiple schools but were working on the preliminary assumption they were hoaxes Image: Carsten Rehder/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools. They said that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats. More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning. What did police say about the bomb threats? Police in Erfurt in Thuringia were among the first to issue a statement on the threats, saying they were responding to threats at "multiple schools" after morning warnings, including in Jena, Erfurt, Mühlhausen, Zella-Mehlis, Nordhausen, Gotha, Rudolstadt and Greiz. "The same word-for-word threats were received this morning at the various eductional institutes," police wrote in a press release . "Based on preliminary findings other federal states are also affected by the threatening messages." Police said they had no information yet on the potential author or sender of the emails. They were investigating breach of the peace-based crimes via the threat of criminal activity. "At present the police is not working on the assumption of the bomb threats being serious and recommends that schools do not implement evacuation measures and continue their normal operations," they said. Police in Freiburg in the southwest and authorities to the north in Hanover also said they were responding to emailed bomb threats directed against schools. Similar reports are emerging to the north of Germany in Denmark . As in Germany, Danish police said they did not believe the threats were credible, "but they understandably create insecurity locally at the schools." Various disruptive incidents targeting Europe in recent weeks This follows other recent cases of coordinated bomb threats against multiple schools that turned out to be hoaxes in Italy earlier in the month. It also comes amid various apparent bids to create disruption within Europe in recent weeks, such as multiple bomb threats targeting commercial airlines , or hacking into supermarket refrigeration systems to spoil produce en masse .
